content: User reported that VPN authentication succeeded after MFA approval, but the tunnel did not establish. Support verified the user account was active, confirmed the VPN client was one minor version behind, flushed DNS, restarted the client, and tested from a second network. Resolution was to update the VPN client and clear the cached profile. Root cause was a stale VPN profile created before the gateway certificate rotation.

metadata.title: VPN Connection Fails After MFA Approval

content: A user could reset the password but was immediately locked out again when signing in to email. Support checked identity logs and found repeated attempts from an old mobile mail profile. Resolution was to remove the stale mobile profile, revoke active sessions, unlock the account, and have the user sign in with the new password. Root cause was cached credentials on an unmanaged mobile client.

metadata.title: Password Reset Loop After Account Unlock

content: Finance users reported delayed outbound email to an approved vendor. Mail trace showed messages held by a data loss prevention rule because attachments matched the finance export pattern. Security reviewed the vendor approval record and released the messages. Permanent fix was to add the vendor domain to the approved finance transfer policy with quarterly review.

metadata.title: Outbound Email Delayed by DLP Rule

content: An analyst requested read access to the curated finance schema. The request was paused because it did not include approval from the finance data owner. Support instructed the requester to attach the approved access form, confirm business purpose, and specify expiration date. Access was granted for 90 days after approval and logged in the access register.

metadata.title: Database Access Request Missing Data Owner Approval

content: A Docker image build failed during private package download with a 401 response. The pipeline secret had expired after rotation. Resolution was to update the package registry token in the CI secret store and rerun the build. Prevention is to monitor token expiry dates and use service account credentials where supported.

metadata.title: Docker Build Fails on Private Package Download

content: The ingestion worker pod entered CrashLoopBackOff after a config map update. Logs showed the worker could not parse the new batch_size value because it was set to text instead of an integer. Resolution was to correct the config map, restart the deployment, and add validation to the Helm values file.

metadata.title: Kubernetes Pod CrashLoopBackOff After Config Change

content: Purpose: restore VPN connectivity for internal users. Prerequisites: identity admin lookup, VPN gateway status dashboard, and user device information. Procedure: confirm the user can complete MFA, verify the account is active, check VPN client version, flush DNS, restart the client, test from another network, and inspect gateway status. Validation: user can authenticate and establish the tunnel. Escalate to Network Operations if authentication succeeds but tunnel creation fails.

Purpose: restore failed scheduled backups for PostgreSQL services. Prerequisites: database read access, backup job dashboard access, and permission to rerun the job. Procedure: confirm the failed job id, inspect storage capacity, verify database connectivity, rerun the backup with the standard profile, and validate that the backup artifact exists. Rollback is not required for a failed backup rerun. Escalate to Data Platform if storage errors continue after capacity is available.

Purpose: recover failed production Airflow DAGs. Procedure: identify the failed task, inspect task logs, check upstream dataset availability, verify connection credentials, clear only the failed task when inputs are valid, and monitor downstream tasks. Rollback: pause the DAG if repeated retries can duplicate downstream writes. Escalate to Data Engineering if source data is missing or schema changed unexpectedly.

Purpose: coordinate response to high severity CVEs affecting managed services. Procedure: confirm affected component and version, map exposed services, check vendor remediation, assign owner team, test the patch in staging, deploy during the approved window, and validate version after deployment. Escalate to Security Operations for internet-facing critical vulnerabilities or active exploitation evidence.

All internal users must use multi-factor authentication for VPN, email, cloud consoles, and privileged access systems. Exceptions require approval from Security Operations and must expire within 30 days. Audit evidence includes MFA enrollment status, exception approvals, and access logs. Users who lose a device must contact IT Support for identity verification before MFA reset.

Production database backups must be retained for 35 days. Monthly compliance snapshots must be retained for 13 months. Backup restoration tests must run at least quarterly and evidence must include job id, restore timestamp, validation query, and owner approval. Exceptions require Data Platform manager approval and must document business risk.

Cloud console access requires manager approval, data owner approval for production data systems, MFA enrollment, and completion of privileged access training. Access must use named accounts and time-bound roles. Shared administrator accounts are prohibited. Reviews occur monthly for privileged roles and quarterly for read-only roles.

Customer data is classified as restricted when it includes direct identifiers, contact details, or account activity. Data owners must define approved use cases, retention, masking requirements, and access review cadence. PII must be masked in analytics sandboxes unless an approved exception exists. Data quality incidents must be logged when completeness or freshness breaches published SLAs.

Summary: after VPN gateway certificate rotation, some clients retained stale profiles and failed tunnel creation after MFA. Impact: 42 remote users could not connect for 55 minutes. Detection: IT support ticket spike and gateway metrics. Root cause: client profile cache did not refresh after certificate replacement. Mitigation: publish profile refresh instructions and push updated client configuration. Prevention: add a pre-rotation test group and post-change client cache validation.

Summary: the daily analytics DAG missed its 08:00 SLA. Impact: finance dashboard refresh was delayed by 90 minutes. Detection: SLA alert from Airflow. Root cause: upstream raw transactions table arrived late after a source system maintenance window. Mitigation: rerun the transform after source completion. Permanent fix: add source availability sensor and notify finance when upstream delay exceeds 30 minutes.

New data engineers must install Git, Python 3.11 or later, Docker Desktop, database client tools, and the approved IDE. They must request access to the development database, Airflow staging, source control organization, and secrets manager. Validation: clone the onboarding repository, run the local test suite, connect to the development database, and trigger the sample Airflow DAG in staging.

Status: accepted. Context: the MVP needs metadata, query logs, evaluation results, and vector search without operating a separate vector database. Decision: use PostgreSQL with pgvector for documents, chunks, embeddings, feedback, and evaluation tables. Options considered: standalone vector database, Elasticsearch only, and PostgreSQL plus pgvector. Consequence: simpler local deployment and strong metadata filtering, with possible scaling work later.

metadata.title: ADR: Use PostgreSQL and pgvector for MVP Retrieval

content: Q: Who approves production database access? A: The data owner and the requester manager must approve production database access. Q: How long should temporary access last? A: Temporary access should include an expiration date and normally lasts 30 to 90 days. Q: What happens if approval is missing? A: IT pauses the request and asks for the missing approval evidence. Q: Where is access recorded? A: Approved access is recorded in the access register.

Q: What should support check first for VPN failures? A: Confirm MFA completion, account status, client version, DNS resolution, and gateway status. Q: What causes repeated password lockouts? A: Stale credentials on mobile clients, mapped drives, or old mail profiles are common causes. Q: What should be checked for delayed email? A: Mail trace, DLP rules, vendor approval, and attachment classification should be reviewed.
